newsitem.title: USA: Vermont senator ready to sacrifice state utilities.
newsitem.headline: Vermont senator ready to sacrifice state utilities.

text.p: The ranking Democrat in the Vermont Senate on Thursday said it would not make sense to restructure the state's investor-owned utilities if they failed to slash costs in their Hydro Quebec contracts.
"I'm willing to sacrifice the utilities if they have to be sacrificed to get lower rates," Senate President Pro-temp Peter Schumlin told reporters.

Schumlin wants shareholders of the companies to "help pay the costs of the bad decisions and contracts that they made....If they can't succeed. then one of the options for any company that makes bad decisions is failure," he said.
The Vermont Senate's floor debate on restructuring in the electricity industry is scheduled for later this month.
Lawmakers are looking into a restructuring and deregulation of the industry to allow competition and lower costs.
The Senate Finance Committee held a hearing on Wednesday night to gauge public opinion about restructuring. It heard mostly from the employees of the utility companies.
The employees said they wanted to add provisions to the measure that would protect displaced workers.
Workers from the Vermont Yankee plant, owned in part by Northeast Utilities, were especially concerned as deregulation would probably make it difficult for nuclear power companies to compete.

"I'm here more for the concern of language added to your legislation...I'm concerned about the employees that it the deregulation will affect. I may be one of them," said Tim Watkins, who works at Vermont Yankee.
